hero.headline: Beyond the Restroom: 30-Day Return-to-Work OS
hero.subheadline: The 30 Days Before and After Maternity Leave Ends - Rights, Pumping Logistics and the Evening Bridge
hero.body: Return date is ~30 days out; nothing is prepared: no freezer bank, no pump-space agreement, no childcare backup, no morning system; she oscillates between denial and 2am panic. A dated operating system for the return: rights-backed ask locked in writing, feeding lane chosen, freezer bank built, mornings drilled - week one becomes execution, not improvisation.
hero.trust_line: Educational content - not medical or legal advice.
hero.evidence_label: Educational content informed by sourced research and clinical guidance. It is not a substitute for medical, clinical, or mental-health assessment.

before_state.label: Sound familiar?
paragraphs: Right now you are avoiding thinking about the date, pump bought but boxed, no written employer request, and evenings scrolling 'should I quit' threads.
It feels like sunday-night dread daily, guilt pre-load, and identity whiplash.
The cost: week-one chaos predicted, supply vulnerable to skipped blocks, and partner load unrenegotiated.
before_state.punch: This is not a personal failing. It is a system gap - and Beyond the Restroom: 30-Day Return-to-Work OS closes it.

modules.label: What Beyond the Restroom: 30-Day Return-to-Work OS gives you
modules.intro: 5 components. One written system. Work through them in order, or jump straight to what today needs.

items.title: The 30-Day Return-to-Work Guide + rights block
items.description: "Going back to work" advice is either corporate HR boilerplate or vague "self-care." Meanwhile the actual problems - pumping at work, the morning hand-off, supply logistics, guilt

items.title: Feeding-at-Work Decision Card
items.description: Re-read your rights block in the Guide. Respond in writing: "Happy to solve logistics together - my request matches [PUMP Act 2022 / HSE guidance / company policy]." Escalation pat

items.title: Red flags & rescue routing (in guide/checklist)
items.description: A bad day does not erase your system. It activates Minimum Mode. You do not "make up" for a lost day. You run the smaller system and continue.

before_after.label: What changes
after_items: Negotiates adjustments from legal footing in writing
Executes three daily anchors (hand-off, blocks, bridge)

for_items: Employed/breastfeeding mother in the final month of maternity leave, dreading the return - pumping logistics, the morning hand-off, supply drop fear, guilt math - with no plan beyond a start date
Return date is ~30 days out; nothing is prepared: no freezer bank, no pump-space agreement, no childcare backup, no morning system; she oscillates between denial and 2am panic
Tried to 'just wing it and see'; or over-bought gadgets without a system; asked other mothers and got contradictory war stories
who_for.not_for_label: This is NOT for you if
not_for_items: Coordinates logistics, rights communication and routines ONLY. Never provides medical advice on mastitis/supply beyond routing to clinicians, never legal representation, never diagnoses PPD.

If any red flag is present (mastitis signs (red hot wedge/fever/flu-feel) = clinician same day; supply collapse across 3+ days = lactation support; persistent hopelessness/dread = clinical support + crisis lines), this is not a home system - seek professional care first.
